title: Painting the Moment
paragraphs: Impressionism began in Paris in the nineteenth century, when a group of painters decided to leave the studio and work outdoors. Instead of slowly polishing a scene in the studio, they tried to capture the changing light of a single moment. Their brushstrokes were quick and visible, and their colours often looked bright and fresh. A reviewer of their first exhibition even described the painters as lunatics.

Practical inventions made this new way of working possible. Ready-made paint sold in tubes meant that artists could work outdoors, and they could also work much faster. Landscapes and scenes of modern city life, painted in bright, pure colours, became typical. Speed mattered, because the light outdoors changes quickly.

The name of the movement came from the title of a painting by Claude Monet, which was shown in 1874. After an exhibition in 1874, the word Impressionist was first used as an insult against the whole group. Over time, the painters became known by that name. Their search for light and the passing moment still shows in their work. Today, their paintings are widely admired.
